title: Crossing the lake: the boat gig, band house and camaraderie
summary: The band traveled by Ford and the lake boat, played for tips on the boat, shared a rented house and cooked together, and always agreed with each other.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: How did you all travel in those days?
Well we had an old car. We used to double up in there. Old Ford car. That's what we used to travel in.
And when you'd go back and forth on the lake, did you take the boat usually? Or?
You mean when we'd go to the lake from here?
Across the lake, like the Covenant, of course you lived over there too.

We lived it over there, yeah. But you see we used to go across on the boat, that camellia, they had a camellia boat what I was telling you about, you see. And that's the time which then people would pay our way on the boat, you see, to come home and go back. You know what I mean? And now's the time the man, the captain of the boat, he wouldn't take our money to come on that boat. He just let us ride because we had a big name over there and he used to come to the dances where we used to play all the time. And what made him did that because one time we came across on that boat and they had a whole lot of people on there. So he came to Buddy and said, hey Buddy, how about you all knocking a little piece there, man, wake it up on this boat. So he said, all right, all right, we'll do that. So man, we took out our instrument, man, we started playing on that boat there and the war, on the war that music sounds good, you know. And boy, them people, man, they come there and they start putting money in our hat. They took one of our hats, you know, put it down there. And man, we start putting money in there. So that's where after we finished playing, the captain said, play one more, buddy, one more. That's all, that's all. We played one more. So all them people, every time we play a number you get that, you know. I said to myself, well I'll be doggone all this money is flying around in the house. That time money was money. You know what I mean? It's plenty of money now but it don't mean nothing now. You know what I mean? Buy a number. So that's where you all, but what Buddy did, Buddy said, well, we're going to stay on this boat till we get over. I said, okay. But one thing about it, if one man would say something, the rest would agree. You know, I've been in lots of bands, if one man would say something like that, the other guy would tell you, say, well man, we better not do that or I don't want to do it. You know what I mean? One guy is always contrary to the rest. You always got along good the whole bunch together. Yeah. But that band there, I must say myself, everybody was agree. I see we went out one night, just want to have fun, and went out the whole band. There's a guy they call Antwine Griffins, he had a restaurant down the street, you know, from where we live. So we said, we go down there and play down there, wake them up. So we liked it to play. And we went down there, man, and boy, a little while after that, that place was like that, and we started playing. That man took my soul out all the stuff that he had to sell, you know, and soft drinks and all that. Well he gave us two dollars a piece. But I mean that was money, you know what I mean? At that time, sure man. You had fun to do with it I guess, or you wouldn't have gone in the first place. Yeah, but I see the way we did out there, we had our own house out there. You know, we rent a house, and we had it all furnished off and everything like that. And we didn't have no women's at all. We used to do our own cooking even in the house, you know. That's the way we used to live out there. That's why I tell you we stayed out there a long time. Yeah, we did a whole lot of cooking out there, because that's the time my old buddy managed to get the banjo player there. He'd get up there and go out to the store and get lots of stuff and come on, because we all gave him the money, we'd chip in so much, and he'd go out there and get all that stuff and come back there and cook that stuff up there.
